edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De praescriptionibus adversus haereticos, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Age nunc, omnes erraverint; deceptus sit Apostolus de testimonio reddendo quibusdam; nullam respexerit Spiritus Sanctus, uti eam in veritatem deduceret, ad hoc missus a Christo, ad hoc postulatus de Patre, ut esset doctor veritatis; neglexerit officium Dei villicus, Christi vicarius, sinens Ecclesias aliter interim intelligere, aliter credere, quam ipse per Apostolos praedicabat: ecquid verisimile est, ut tot ac tantae in unam fidem erraverint? Nullus inter multos eventus unus est exitus: variasse debuerat error doctrinae Ecclesiarum. Caeterum, quod apud multos unum invenitur, non est erratum, sed traditum. Audeat ergo aliquis dicere illos errasse qui tradiderunt?
pass_a_gloss: Now come, let all have erred; let the Apostle have been deceived about giving testimony to certain people; let the Holy Spirit have looked back at no one, so that He might lead that one into truth, sent for this purpose by Christ, requested for this purpose from the Father, so that He might be the teacher of truth; let the steward of God, the vicar of Christ, have neglected his duty, allowing the Churches to understand and believe otherwise in the meantime, than what He Himself was preaching through the Apostles: is it likely that so many and such great ones have erred into one faith? There is not one outcome among many events: the error of the doctrine of the Churches ought to have varied. Meanwhile, what is found to be one among many is not something that has been erred, but something that has been handed down. Therefore, let someone dare to say that those who handed down erred.
pass_b_english: Go ahead: suppose everyone got it wrong. Suppose the Apostle was duped when he bore witness to certain people. Suppose the Holy Spirit never glanced back to guide anyone into truth, even though Christ sent Him for that very purpose and the Father dispatched Him to be the teacher of truth. Suppose the steward of God, the vicar of Christ, neglected his job and let the churches understand and believe something different in the meantime from what He Himself had preached through the Apostles. Is it really plausible that so many and such great churches all erred their way into a single faith? Among many events there is not a single outcome; the error of the churches' doctrine should have varied. Yet what is found to be one and the same among many is not an error—it is a tradition. So let anyone dare to claim that the ones who handed it down were wrong.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the conditional/subjunctive mood of the Latin 'erraverint', 'deceptus sit', etc., as a series of hypothetical concessions. Pass B provides a more idiomatic rendering of these concessions ('Suppose...') while maintaining the semantic integrity of the Latin. All clauses in the Latin source are accounted for in both Pass A and Pass B.
